body: This is very likely due to the block cache memtracker being deleted (no remaining shared_ptr left) -- assigning a copy of the pointer to a static variable to keep it alive appears to fix it. Unsure at the moment why there are sometimes no more references to the pointer.

issue.title: [DocDB] Version 2.17.1.0 does not display BlockBasedTable in mem-trackers page

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-5478](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-5478)
### Description

YB version: `version 2.17.1.0 build 439 revision 8a09a531b55a0564fc186f69e93d5c56fb0f8b67 build_type RELEASE built at 03 Feb 2023 22:14:11 UTC`
OS: Alma 8.7 x86_64

With version 2.17.1.0b439, the BlockBasedTable is gone from the /mem-trackers page (see [1]).
When checking with version 2.17.0.0 (`version 2.17.0.0 build 24 revision d4f01a5e26b168585e59f9c1a95766ffdd9655b1 build_type RELEASE built at 16 Nov 2022 00:21:52 UTC`), the block based table is visible (see [2]).

When using the statistics, it is visible that in 2.17.1.0b439, the BlockBasedTable is actually used:
```
$ yb_stats --gauges-enable --hostname-match 9000 --details-enable --table-name-match '^t$'`
Begin ad-hoc in-memory snapshot created, press enter to create end snapshot for difference calculation.

Time between snapshots:    1.344 seconds

192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     mem_tracker_BlockBasedTable_RegularDB                                            25944 bytes               +0
192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     mem_tracker_IntentsDB                                                         22153216 bytes               +0
192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     mem_tracker_IntentsDB_MemTable                                                22153216 bytes               +0
192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     mem_tracker_RegularDB                                                         17238016 bytes               +0
192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     mem_tracker_RegularDB_MemTable                                                17238016 bytes               +0
192.168.66.80:9000   tablet   d658eb021e5148068676b649c6fbefd6 yugabyte.t                     raft_term                                                                            1 terms               +0
```
So it seems they are simply omitted from the mem-trackers page.
